source_adaptation: I14 specifies an encounter window rather than the earlier fixed teaching sequence. The 5/5/20/7/3 classroom plan is an authoring guide, not a scheme timing claim. Arrange a reasonable period for the actual provider during the school day; extend or separate that window if needed. Visitor, recorded-talk and no-visitor routes share preparation and reflection. Profile practice and recorded information without provider interaction are not a completed real encounter.
success: Ask a question that has a clear purpose.
Record recruitment/entry information and gaps accurately.
Link evidence about one route to an own need, with judgement and next question.
prepare: Books, pens, question menu, recording structure, normal reading/typing aids and fallback profiles A/B. Preview any approved local recording and arrange captions or a transcript. No recording, visitor or live link is supplied or assumed. If neither visitor nor recording is ready, use the complete profile simulation.
activity: Prepare a purposeful question, model fact/gap recording and rehearse. Use a visitor, recorded talk or full profile simulation with appropriate response-status logging. Immediately evaluate one route against an own need, give feedback, fade prompts and reflect.

evidence.description: Provider encounter log with evaluation and next question: purposeful question and actual asking/relay status, recruitment/entry facts and gaps, source/mode and actual response status, own need linked to route evidence, reasoned judgement and next question. Retain support and revision. Simulated skill evidence and hypothetical needs are explicitly distinguished from a real provider encounter and own-needs evidence.

evidence_detail: Provider encounter log with evaluation and next question: purposeful question and actual asking/relay status, recruitment/entry facts and gaps, source/mode and actual response status, own need linked to route evidence, reasoned judgement and next question. Retain support and revision. Simulated skill evidence and hypothetical needs are explicitly distinguished from a real provider encounter and own-needs evidence.
assessment: N14 is F + S: formative preparation/questioning plus retained evaluation evidence. Week 7 remains the assessing week. J14 requires an encounter log with evaluation and next question. Keep the question, whether/how it was asked, actual recruitment/entry information, source/mode, own need, evidence-based judgement, limit and next question. Record support and revision. In fallback mode this is simulated skill evidence; the actual encounter end check remains not yet.
boundaries: No named provider, organisation, institution or live address in the pack. Profiles are invented and cannot verify actual eligibility, pay, grades, places or support. Use actual session information only when heard and attributable to the selected source; keep gaps. No application, contact or disclosure is required from pupils. No recording or visitor is claimed to have occurred.
feedback: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E evidence recorded; R responded. Set one precise next step. R requires Voice and Audience, NS and learner response in in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. A private adult may be the audience. E only for actual banked evidence.
response_modes: Book first. Type instead gives the same record. Private own-needs responses are available. A hypothetical need can show rehearsal but not the own-needs component. Reader, scribe, typing and adult relay of a learner-authored question are normal access, with actual answer prompts logged separately.

routes.Independent: Choose a route/enquiry and an own need, ask a purposeful question, record recruitment/entry facts and gaps, then evaluate one route with evidence. Give a qualified judgement and next question. Check the source mode and whether a provider response actually occurred.
routes.Supported: Use one profile or talk section at a time. Offer the six-topic menu, a separate model, vocabulary and record headings. Rehearse privately and allow a learner-authored written question to be relayed. Keep all three parts of the outcome; fade answer prompts where secure.
routes.Floor: Use profile A and the short choices. Read aloud or scribe the learner’s own answers. Help them select, then actually ask or relay, a question in practice. Record the application step and an entry gap. Add one own need and a reasoned fit. Choice answers alone do not establish the full outcome or real encounter.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Explicit instruction, worked model and guided practice. Chunk the talk/profile and use question, fact, gap, need and judgement headings. Repeat key points and allow processing time. Use the written profile as memory support.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Pre-teach provider, recruitment, entry, support and evaluate. Rehearse privately. Accept speech, writing, pointing, scribe or adult relay of the learner’s own question. Check that the learner can access the response. No cold calling.
adaptations.SEMH: Explain who will speak, how questions work and the right to pause. No public disclosure of grades, health, family work or income. A learning need may be shared privately. Offer a regulation break with an agreed return point. A route judgement can be tentative.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Use clear print, captions/transcript, normal aids and an accessible question method. Check hearing, sightlines and processing in advance. Do not infer route suitability from diagnosis or support needs; ask which support could help.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pre-teach the topic words and offer short frames. Pause or replay a recording where helpful. Separate language access from evaluation. Retain normal access while answer scaffolds fade.

hinge: The speaker did not give entry grades. Which record is accurate? A: Make a likely grade up. B: Write “not stated” and keep a question. Answer B. Ask for the source clue. If insecure, separate known, assumed and missing, model again and use the parallel hinge.
parallel_hinge: A recorded talk is played but no provider answers learner questions. Which log fits? A: Real two-way provider encounter complete. B: Recorded information used; provider reply pending. Answer B. Re-model activity mode versus actual response. Retain supported recording if insecure.
frames: F: “What do I need to ... ?” M: “I ask this because ... . The source says ... . It does not say ... .” H: “I need ... . This route could fit because ... , but ... . Before deciding I would ask ... .”
misconceptions: “An unanswered detail can be guessed.” Keep it as a gap. “Watching a talk or teacher role-play proves a real encounter.” Record actual provider interaction separately. “Offered support guarantees every adjustment.” Confirm the specific arrangement. “A positive judgement means I am eligible.” It is a reason to investigate, not admission.
ta_focus: Model: check the question’s purpose. Encounter: help access/relay the learner’s question, record actual words and response without inventing. Evaluation: prompt the evidence-to-need link and fade. Ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return the task.
worked_example_and_fade: Practice need: I learn best with written steps. Purposeful question: “How can I get written steps for a task?” Profile A offers written steps and weekly tutor check-ins. Record the source as simulated A. Evaluation: “This could fit the practice need, but other support and travel are unknown. I would ask how support is agreed.” Recruitment: application, discussion and short task; exact grades not given. Fade to the learner choosing a different need or profile and making their own judgement.
check_after_model: Which is more useful: “Is this good?” or “What happens in the entry task?” Expected: the second gives a specific recruitment detail. Does an unanswered question mean a place or support is guaranteed? No. Record pending or not stated.

delivery_modes.Visitor mode: Brief the visitor on content, assessment, employer links, support, entry/recruitment and progression. Explain learner questions and agreed access. Give every learner a way to ask or relay their question and receive a response. Allow a follow-up. Record what was actually said and any unknown detail.
delivery_modes.Recorded talk mode: Use an already approved recording with captions/transcript. Pause to record facts and prepare questions. Arrange a genuine provider response opportunity through staff if possible. Until it occurs, mark questions pending and provider interaction not yet. A class discussion of a recording alone is not a provider reply.
delivery_modes.No visitor or recording mode: Read profile A or B, then let an adult role-play answers from the printed response bank. Clearly label the activity simulated. Unknown answers remain unknown. Complete the same record and evaluation as skill practice. Keep a question for a future real encounter; do not award encounter completion for the role-play.

provider_profiles.content: Practical making and repair. Learn to measure, follow plans and check finished work. No practical task is carried out in this lesson.
provider_profiles.pattern: The sample week has three workshop days and two classroom days. This is only the example timetable.
provider_profiles.assessment: Staff check practical tasks and a short work record. Feedback shows what to improve before the next task.
provider_profiles.employer_link: A workplace project is part of the example. It does not promise a placement or job.
provider_profiles.recruitment: An application is followed by a course discussion and a short reading and measuring task. A place is not automatic.
provider_profiles.entry: The task checks starting skills and support needs. Exact grades, equivalent awards and any age rule are not given. Ask before a real application.
provider_profiles.support: Written steps and a weekly tutor check-in are offered in the example. Other support must be discussed; it is not confirmed by this card.
provider_profiles.progression: After the course, a learner could apply for further technical study, an apprenticeship or trainee work. Each next step has its own entry checks.
provider_profiles.unknown: Start date, application deadline, travel, costs and any place available are not stated.

provider_profiles.content: Work on clear messages, accurate records and planning office tasks. Learn at work with time for training.
provider_profiles.pattern: The sample week has four work days and one training day. Real work and training patterns may differ.
provider_profiles.assessment: A work log and checks of skills show progress. The learner must complete the required final checks.
provider_profiles.employer_link: The apprentice works in an office and has a supervisor. This card describes no real vacancy.
provider_profiles.recruitment: Apply for a vacancy. The sample employer uses an interview and a short office task to select a learner.
provider_profiles.entry: The office task checks clear messages and accurate records. Exact grades, equivalents, English and maths rules and age rules are not supplied.
provider_profiles.support: A supervisor check-in is offered each week in the example. Training support can be discussed. Specific adjustments must be confirmed.
provider_profiles.progression: After training, the learner could seek an admin role or more training. Continued work or promotion is not promised.
provider_profiles.unknown: Pay, contract length, start date, deadline, travel and any vacancy available are not stated.

profile_status: Practice profiles prepared 30 October 2026. These are invented teaching examples, not real providers, places or entry rules.
question_topics: What will I learn or do each week?
How will you check my work and give feedback?
How is an employer involved in this route?
What support can I ask for, and how is it agreed?
What do I need to apply, and how do you select people?
What could I do next, and what would that step need?
record_fields: My question and why it matters
Asked to whom and answer status
My own need and route evidence
own_needs_rule: A learner may share an own need privately. Hypothetical needs show practice only and do not establish the own-needs component. An adult may relay a learner-authored question without changing its meaning.
encounter_evidence_rule: M14: Was the encounter meaningful, two-way and linked to a real decision or enquiry? Record actual provider involvement, accessible question/response opportunity, date, duration and the learner’s enquiry. A prepared question, recording alone or simulation does not confirm this. Responsible staff track year-group entitlement and the source’s Year 9/11/13 timing separately; this pack does not certify statutory completion.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Teacher and cover planner
Provider encounter 1 — technical education/apprenticeships
Tuesday 8 December 2026 · P3 · Year A
GROW · up to five learners · 40-minute classroom plan with flexible encounter window
Unit: Identity & Belonging — Belonging in work
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Exact source outcome
I can ask a purposeful question, record recruitment/entry information and evaluate one route against my own needs.
Weekly outcome: Students use a meaningful provider encounter to test assumptions about technical and apprenticeship routes.

Source: specialist Careers scheme, GROW Careers physical row 14, Autumn 2 row 6. E14 weekly outcome; F14 focus; G14 exact outcome; H14 sequence; I14 encounter window; J14 evidence; K14 access; L14 support; M14 end check; N14 F + S.
Question and success checks
What do I need to ask to judge whether one route could fit my needs?
1. Ask a question that has a clear purpose. 2. Record recruitment/entry information and gaps accurately. 3. Link evidence about one route to my own need, give a judgement and a next question.
Prepare

Books, pens, question menu, recording structure, normal reading/typing aids and fallback profiles A/B. Preview any approved local recording and arrange captions or a transcript. No recording, visitor or live link is supplied or assumed. If neither visitor nor recording is ready, use the complete profile simulation.
Source adaptation

I14 specifies an encounter window rather than the earlier fixed teaching sequence. The 5/5/20/7/3 classroom plan is an authoring guide, not a scheme timing claim. Arrange a reasonable period for the actual provider during the school day; extend or separate that window if needed. Visitor, recorded-talk and no-visitor routes share preparation and reflection. Profile practice and recorded information without provider interaction are not a completed real encounter.
Where this leads
This helps me ask useful questions before a training choice and decide what I need to check next.
Session modes and timing
Phase
Min
Action and evidence
Prepare
Recall entry versus skills learned. Choose one route or enquiry, one own need and one purposeful question from the menu.
Model and rehearse
Model a focused question and a fact/gap record. Rehearse privately or agree an adult relay in the learner’s words.
Encounter or simulation
Use the chosen mode below. Gather recruitment/entry information. Keep time for learner questions, answers and follow-up. Record actual mode and response status.
Evaluate
Immediately judge one route against an own need. Use a source detail, a possible fit or concern and a limit. Give one next step and fade answer prompts.
Reflect
Keep the next question, actual evidence and support. Log real interaction separately from preparation or simulation.

5 + 5 + 20 + 7 + 3 = 40 minutes. This is a planning example. Do not cut meaningful questions to fit it. If the actual encounter needs a separate or longer window, prepare beforehand and evaluate immediately afterwards; record actual date and duration.
Visitor mode

Brief the visitor on content, assessment, employer links, support, entry/recruitment and progression. Explain learner questions and agreed access. Give every learner a way to ask or relay their question and receive a response. Allow a follow-up. Record what was actually said and any unknown detail.
Recorded talk mode

Use an already approved recording with captions/transcript. Pause to record facts and prepare questions. Arrange a genuine provider response opportunity through staff if possible. Until it occurs, mark questions pending and provider interaction not yet. A class discussion of a recording alone is not a provider reply.
No visitor or recording mode

Read profile A or B, then let an adult role-play answers from the printed response bank. Clearly label the activity simulated. Unknown answers remain unknown. Complete the same record and evaluation as skill practice. Keep a question for a future real encounter; do not award encounter completion for the role-play.
Routes and planned access
Independent

Choose a route/enquiry and an own need, ask a purposeful question, record recruitment/entry facts and gaps, then evaluate one route with evidence. Give a qualified judgement and next question. Check the source mode and whether a provider response actually occurred.
Supported

Use one profile or talk section at a time. Offer the six-topic menu, a separate model, vocabulary and record headings. Rehearse privately and allow a learner-authored written question to be relayed. Keep all three parts of the outcome; fade answer prompts where secure.
Floor

Use profile A and the short choices. Read aloud or scribe the learner’s own answers. Help them select, then actually ask or relay, a question in practice. Record the application step and an entry gap. Add one own need and a reasoned fit. Choice answers alone do not establish the full outcome or real encounter.
Cognition and Learning

Explicit instruction, worked model and guided practice. Chunk the talk/profile and use question, fact, gap, need and judgement headings. Repeat key points and allow processing time. Use the written profile as memory support.
Communication and Interaction

Pre-teach provider, recruitment, entry, support and evaluate. Rehearse privately. Accept speech, writing, pointing, scribe or adult relay of the learner’s own question. Check that the learner can access the response. No cold calling.
SEMH

Explain who will speak, how questions work and the right to pause. No public disclosure of grades, health, family work or income. A learning need may be shared privately. Offer a regulation break with an agreed return point. A route judgement can be tentative.
Sensory and Physical

Use clear print, captions/transcript, normal aids and an accessible question method. Check hearing, sightlines and processing in advance. Do not infer route suitability from diagnosis or support needs; ask which support could help.
EAL

Plan in any language. Pre-teach the topic words and offer short frames. Pause or replay a recording where helpful. Separate language access from evaluation. Retain normal access while answer scaffolds fade.

A hypothetical need can support practice without disclosure. Label it hypothetical; the own-needs component remains unconfirmed until the learner offers an own need privately. Do not count a prepared but unasked question as asked.
Staff prompts and checks
Worked example and fade

Practice need: I learn best with written steps. Purposeful question: “How can I get written steps for a task?” Profile A offers written steps and weekly tutor check-ins. Record the source as simulated A. Evaluation: “This could fit the practice need, but other support and travel are unknown. I would ask how support is agreed.” Recruitment: application, discussion and short task; exact grades not given. Fade to the learner choosing a different need or profile and making their own judgement.
Check after the model

Which is more useful: “Is this good?” or “What happens in the entry task?” Expected: the second gives a specific recruitment detail. Does an unanswered question mean a place or support is guaranteed? No. Record pending or not stated.
Hinge during recording

The speaker did not give entry grades. Which record is accurate? A: Make a likely grade up. B: Write “not stated” and keep a question. Answer B. Ask for the source clue. If insecure, separate known, assumed and missing, model again and use the parallel hinge.
Parallel hinge

A recorded talk is played but no provider answers learner questions. Which log fits? A: Real two-way provider encounter complete. B: Recorded information used; provider reply pending. Answer B. Re-model activity mode versus actual response. Retain supported recording if insecure.
Speaking frames
F: “What do I need to ... ?” M: “I ask this because ... . The source says ... . It does not say ... .” H: “I need ... . This route could fit because ... , but ... . Before deciding I would ask ... .”
TA focus and prompt ladder

Model: check the question’s purpose. Encounter: help access/relay the learner’s question, record actual words and response without inventing. Evaluation: prompt the evidence-to-need link and fade. Ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return the task.
Misconceptions and corrections

“An unanswered detail can be guessed.” Keep it as a gap. “Watching a talk or teacher role-play proves a real encounter.” Record actual provider interaction separately. “Offered support guarantees every adjustment.” Confirm the specific arrangement. “A positive judgement means I am eligible.” It is a reason to investigate, not admission.
Evidence and encounter record
What this lesson can evidence

N14 is F + S: formative preparation/questioning plus retained evaluation evidence. Week 7 remains the assessing week. J14 requires an encounter log with evaluation and next question. Keep the question, whether/how it was asked, actual recruitment/entry information, source/mode, own need, evidence-based judgement, limit and next question. Record support and revision. In fallback mode this is simulated skill evidence; the actual encounter end check remains not yet.
Response and feedback

Book first. Type instead gives the same record. Private own-needs responses are available. A hypothetical need can show rehearsal but not the own-needs component. Reader, scribe, typing and adult relay of a learner-authored question are normal access, with actual answer prompts logged separately.

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E evidence recorded; R responded. Set one precise next step. R requires Voice and Audience, NS and learner response in in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. A private adult may be the audience. E only for actual banked evidence.
Meaningful encounter and entitlement

M14: Was the encounter meaningful, two-way and linked to a real decision or enquiry? Record actual provider involvement, accessible question/response opportunity, date, duration and the learner’s enquiry. A prepared question, recording alone or simulation does not confirm this. Responsible staff track year-group entitlement and the source’s Year 9/11/13 timing separately; this pack does not certify statutory completion.
Portfolio

Keep the log, evaluation, next question, source status, support and revision in the Careers Portfolio/action plan. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping from actual work; no completion inferred. Record a follow-up owner/role and review date for unanswered questions, without inventing a response.
Boundaries

No named provider, organisation, institution or live address in the pack. Profiles are invented and cannot verify actual eligibility, pay, grades, places or support. Use actual session information only when heard and attributable to the selected source; keep gaps. No application, contact or disclosure is required from pupils. No recording or visitor is claimed to have occurred.
Calendar and sequence

Year A. Autumn 2 Week 6, 7–11 December 2026. Tuesday 8 December, P3. Flexible encounter window; 40-minute classroom example. Actual event date/duration recorded separately. Week 7 follows after Downloaded and is assessing.

Weekly plan notes

Extend or separate an actual event as needed; prepare before it and evaluate immediately after. Record actual time and staff entitlement checks separately.

Evidence and response

Staff answers and session guide
Outcome and source
I can ask a purposeful question, record recruitment/entry information and evaluate one route against my own needs.

E14 meaningful provider encounter, H14 preparation/two-way questions/immediate evaluation, J14 log and next question, M14 meaningful two-way enquiry, N14 F + S. I14 is a flexible window; it does not give the earlier fixed phase timings. The 40-minute example is 5/5/20/7/3.
Mode decisions
Mode
Valid record
Boundary
Visitor
Learner question/relay, provider reply, follow-up, entry facts and own-needs evaluation.
Record actual interaction; do not infer attendance or entitlement from the plan.
Recorded talk
Attributable information, prepared questions, actual provider response if later arranged.
Playback or classroom discussion alone does not show provider two-way interaction.
Profile fallback
Adult role-play answer from A/B, accurate source label, own-needs evaluation of example.
Simulated skill evidence only; real encounter check remains not yet.
Preparation brief

Agree the enquiry, learning outcome, six topics, question methods and access before an actual event. Preview recording/captions/transcript. Allow reasonable time during the school day; extend or separate the encounter window if needed. Evaluate immediately afterwards. If nothing is available, teach the complete simulation.
Question purpose

A useful question seeks information that could affect an enquiry: entry task, teaching pattern, assessment, support, employer link or next step. “Is it good?” is too broad unless followed by a specific question. The learner may write or relay their own words.
Profile facts and sample evaluations
Practice profiles prepared 30 October 2026. These are invented teaching examples, not real providers, places or entry rules.
Field
A technical course
B office apprenticeship
Content and level
Practical making/repair; Level 2 example.
Office messages, records and planning; Level 3 example.
Week
Three workshop and two classroom days.
Four work and one training day.
Recruitment
Application, course discussion, short reading/measuring task.
Vacancy application, interview, short office task.
Entry gap
Exact grades/equivalents and age rule not stated.
Exact grades/equivalents, English/maths and age rules not stated.
Support
Written steps, weekly tutor check-in; other support to discuss.
Weekly supervisor check-in; training support/adjustments to confirm.
Next step
Further study, apprenticeship or trainee work, with new entry checks.
Seek admin work or training; no continued job promise.
Examples of reasoning

If the learner genuinely needs practical learning: A could fit because three workshop days are described, but the exact tasks and travel need checking. If they need written steps: A offers them in the example; ask how a real course would agree support. If they want work with training: B could fit, but exact hours, support and entry rules remain open.

“Does not fit yet” and “unsure” can be valid with evidence. Do not assume an own need from a diagnosis, task behaviour or copied model. A stated fact plus the learner’s own reason matters more than a positive answer. Sample weeks total five days each, not a general rule.
Checks and misconceptions
After the model
The specific entry-task question is more purposeful than “Is this good?” Unknown support or entry detail is not a promise. Ask for the profile/source clue and preserve gaps.
Main hinge
B: entry grades not stated should be recorded as not stated with a question. If insecure, model known versus guessed versus missing, then use the parallel hinge.
Parallel hinge

B: recording used, provider reply pending. A talk viewed without provider response does not establish two-way interaction. A teacher’s profile reply is simulated even when the learner asks a good question.
Floor

Key A, A, B, A, B, A. Choices alone are insufficient. Gather the actual asked/relayed question, purpose, recruitment/entry facts or stated gaps, own need and evaluation with next question. Distinguish reader/scribe access from answers supplied.
Misconceptions

A prepared question is not yet asked. “Not stated” is accurate only where the source is silent; do not use it instead of listening to a given answer. Offered support does not establish all adjustments. Entry selection is not guaranteed admission. A positive fit judgement is not proof of eligibility. Hypothetical needs and simulated sources must remain labelled.
Privacy and participation

No forced public sharing, personal grades, health, family employment or income. An own need can be a general learning preference, offered privately. A learner can pause and return, use normal aids or ask via an adult. Preserve the learner’s thought and the actual reply.
Evidence and next steps
Core outcome evidence

Question has a clear purpose and is actually asked or relayed. Record recruitment/entry information accurately, including genuine gaps. Evaluate one route against an own need using a source detail, a fit/concern/uncertainty judgement and a reason. Keep a next question. Track actual source/mode so rehearsal is not presented as real provider engagement.
Secure and partial evidence

Secure skill example in fallback: learner asks an entry-task question, records A’s application/discussion/task and missing grades, states an own need for written steps, links A’s support to that need and asks how real support would be agreed. Log it simulated. The real encounter end check is still not yet.

Partial: question written but not asked; guessed grades; no recruitment/entry record; “good” without evidence; copied or hypothetical need presented as own; or simulation logged as a visitor. Separate the missing component from what the learner did demonstrate.
Precise next steps

“Ask or relay the question you prepared.” “Add the selection step the source gave.” “Keep the missing grade as a question.” “Link one detail to your own need.” “Explain why you are unsure.” Set one next step and retain the response.
Source end check and entitlement

M14 asks whether the encounter was meaningful, two-way and linked to a real decision/enquiry. Actual provider participation and accessible response opportunity must be evidenced. Track year-group entitlement and source timing requirements separately through responsible staff. No lesson sheet certifies compliance. Recorded-only and simulated modes remain preparation or skill practice until a real encounter is established.
Portfolio and feedback

N14 F + S retained: formative preparation with recorded evaluation evidence. Week 7 assessing. Retain log, source/mode, question status, needs type, actual support and revision. Offer to the Communication portfolio. E for actual banked evidence; R after Voice, Audience, NS and response in in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Any accredited mapping requires staff confirmation from actual work.
Profile A Technical college course
Practice profiles prepared 30 October 2026. These are invented teaching examples, not real providers, places or entry rules.
Level: Level 2 in this example
Learning and assessment
Practical making and repair. Learn to measure, follow plans and check finished work. No practical task is carried out in this lesson.
The sample week has three workshop days and two classroom days. This is only the example timetable.
Staff check practical tasks and a short work record. Feedback shows what to improve before the next task.
Employer link
A workplace project is part of the example. It does not promise a placement or job.
Recruitment and entry
An application is followed by a course discussion and a short reading and measuring task. A place is not automatic.
The task checks starting skills and support needs. Exact grades, equivalent awards and any age rule are not given. Ask before a real application.
Support
Written steps and a weekly tutor check-in are offered in the example. Other support must be discussed; it is not confirmed by this card.
Next steps and gaps
After the course, a learner could apply for further technical study, an apprenticeship or trainee work. Each next step has its own entry checks.
Start date, application deadline, travel, costs and any place available are not stated.
Choose a question that helps you judge this route. Say what you still need to know.
Profile B Office apprenticeship
Practice profiles prepared 30 October 2026. These are invented teaching examples, not real providers, places or entry rules.
Level: Level 3 in this example
Learning and assessment
Work on clear messages, accurate records and planning office tasks. Learn at work with time for training.
The sample week has four work days and one training day. Real work and training patterns may differ.
A work log and checks of skills show progress. The learner must complete the required final checks.
Employer link
The apprentice works in an office and has a supervisor. This card describes no real vacancy.
Recruitment and entry
Apply for a vacancy. The sample employer uses an interview and a short office task to select a learner.
The office task checks clear messages and accurate records. Exact grades, equivalents, English and maths rules and age rules are not supplied.
Support
A supervisor check-in is offered each week in the example. Training support can be discussed. Specific adjustments must be confirmed.
Next steps and gaps
After training, the learner could seek an admin role or more training. Continued work or promotion is not promised.
Pay, contract length, start date, deadline, travel and any vacancy available are not stated.
Choose a question that helps you judge this route. Say what you still need to know.
Questions with a purpose
Choose one question that helps with your enquiry. You can change the words. Say why the answer would help you.
Topic
Question idea
Content
What will I learn or do each week?
Assessment
How will you check my work and give feedback?
Employer link
How is an employer involved in this route?
Support
What support can I ask for, and how is it agreed?
Entry and recruitment
What do I need to apply, and how do you select people?
Progression
What could I do next, and what would that step need?
Before the session
“I need ... . I want to find out ... . My question is ... .” You may keep your own need private.
During the session
Ask or agree for an adult to relay your own question. Listen to the answer. Write a short fact, then what is still unknown. Ask a follow-up if needed.
After the session
Choose one route. Link a fact to your own need. Give a fit, a concern or an unsure judgement with a reason. Keep one next question.
Mark the source: visitor, recording or practice profile. A question can be prepared, asked or still pending. A reply from a teacher in role-play is a practice reply.
A model and short choices
Practice example

Practice need: I learn best with written steps. Question: “How can I get written steps for a task?” A offers written steps and a weekly tutor check-in. This could fit, but travel and other support are unknown. Next question: “How do we agree the support I need?”
A recruitment note: application, discussion and a short task. Exact entry grades are not stated. This is profile practice, not a real offer.
Floor choices
Use profile A. An adult may read or scribe your own choices.
Check
Choices
Purposeful question
A: What happens in the entry task? B: Is it good?
Recruitment
A: Apply, then discussion and short task. B: A place is automatic.
Missing grades
A: Guess them. B: Write not stated and ask.
Recorded talk only
A: A provider reply is still needed. B: All questions have been answered.
Own need
A: Copy the model as my own view. B: Give my own need privately or label practice.
Evaluation
A: Link a source fact to a need and keep a question. B: Say best with no reason.
“I need ... . The source says ... . This could fit because ... , but ... . I would ask ... .”
The choices alone are not the full task. Ask your question and record a reply or gap. Give a reason about one route. Plan in any language.
Adult response bank for practice
Use only for the profile simulation. Tell learners that the adult is role-playing. Answer from A or B, then ask if the reply helped. Do not invent a missing fact.

Let the learner ask a follow-up. Log the adult reply as simulated, never as external provider contact. Do not complete entitlement records from role-play.
Adult key and evidence boundary
Keep this page apart from first choices. Record the learner’s own answers before showing the key.
Check

Purposeful question
A: The entry task question has a clear information purpose.
Recruitment
A: Profile A lists application, discussion and a short task.

Floor key A, A, B, A, B, A. Also retain the actual question, asking/relay status, recruitment/entry record and reasoned evaluation. Prepared alone is not asked. A guessed fact is not evidence.

A practice need can show how to reason but does not establish the own-needs part. Offer a private response without pressure. Fallback skill evidence does not establish a real provider encounter. Record the next opportunity as not yet, not completed.
Words for a provider encounter
Word
Meaning
provider
A group that offers education or training.
technical education
Learning skills and knowledge for a type of work.
apprenticeship
A job that includes planned training.
purposeful question
A question asked for a clear reason.
recruitment
The process of finding and selecting people.
entry information
What you need and how to start a route.
assessment
A way to check learning or skills.
support
Help or changes that may make learning possible.
progression
A next step in learning, work or responsibility.
evidence
A detail that supports what you say.
evaluate
Weigh evidence to make a reasoned judgement.
two-way
Both sides can take part and respond.
simulation
Practice that represents an event.
pending
Waiting to happen or waiting for a reply.
Words for my judgement
I need ... . The source says ... . This could fit because ... . I still need to ask ... .

weekly_plan_row.objective_verbatim: I can ask a purposeful question, record recruitment/entry information and evaluate one route against my own needs.
weekly_plan_row.encounter_window: Actual provider period flexible; record actual date/duration. Preparation before, evaluation immediately afterwards.
weekly_plan_row.evidence: Provider encounter log with evaluation and next question: purposeful question and actual asking/relay status, recruitment/entry facts and gaps, source/mode and actual response status, own need linked to route evidence, reasoned judgement and next question.
